svg.aria-label: How to write buenos días: 10 letters, b, u, e, n, o, s, d, í, a, s, one after another
svg.title: Writing buenos días
svg.desc: 10 letters written one after another: b, u, e, n, o, s, d, í, a, s (latin). Each letter has its own group of frames; frame N of a group shows movements 1 to N of that letter, the movement being added drawn in ink over the finished letter, whose outline is read from _fonts/LatinPrint-Subset.ttf. Each letter is drawn at its own scale from its own cited stroke order, so the strip does not show how large the letters are next to each other, how far apart they sit, or any join between them. Stroke order: b: Grundschrift-App (Laborschule Bielefeld, Bielefeld University, with the Grundschulverband), level kleinbuchstaben/b, ordered stroke paths for b (assets/levels/kleinbuchstaben/b/metadata.json, commit f6dbd80; no licence, facts only) <https://github.com/Medien-Treibhaus/grundschrift-app-source/blob/f6dbd807adbb3fc2f94207fe578def439f6e9c49/assets/levels/kleinbuchstaben/b/metadata.json>; u: Grundschrift-App (Laborschule Bielefeld, Bielefeld University, with the Grundschulverband), level kleinbuchstaben/u, ordered stroke paths for u (assets/levels/kleinbuchstaben/u/metadata.json, commit f6dbd80; Source notes on variation: b: The Grundschrift-App was made in a research project of the Laborschule at Bielefeld University with the Grundschulverband, on its Grundschrift school model, with a teacher advisory team. Each letter is an ordered list of paths, one per pen-down stroke, which the app makes a child trace in order. It writes b in one stroke: down the stem from the top, back up it, and clockwise round the bowl to the foot of the stem. UJIpenchars2 (Prat, Castro, Llorens, Marzal and Vilar; UCI Machine Learning Repository dataset 177, CC BY 4.0) holds 120 tablet pen traces of b, two by each of 60 adult Spanish writers; only counts are cited. 115 of the 120 are one stroke, the source's count, and 75 of those 115 start at the top left (24 start at the bottom left, as a joined hand does). The app's repository has no licence, so only the order, the start, the direction and the lifts are taken from it; no point is copied, and the path is fitted to the b of the bundled LatinPrint-Subset.ttf, a renamed subset of SIL Global's literacy typeface Andika 7.000, which prints the one-storey a the school model teaches; the book's own text face is a different font. Handwriting varies by writer. u: The Grundschrift-App was made in a research project of the Laborschule at Bielefeld University with the Grundschulverband, on its Grundschrift school model, with a teacher advisory team. Each letter is an ordered list of paths, one per pen-down stroke, which the app makes a child trace in order. It writes u in one stroke: down from the top left, round the bottom and up, then down the right side. Grundschrift ends the stroke with a small hook to the right that the bundled outline does not print, so the path ends where the printed letter ends. UJIpenchars2 (Prat, Castro, Llorens, Marzal and Vilar; UCI Machine Learning Repository dataset 177, CC BY 4.0) holds 120 tablet pen traces of u, two by each of 60 adult Spanish writers; only counts are cited. All 120 are one stroke, and 85 start at the top left. The app's repository has no licence, so only the order, the start, the direction and the lifts are taken from it; no point is copied, and the path is fitted to the u of the bundled LatinPrint-Subset.ttf, a renamed subset of SIL Global's literacy typeface Andika 7.000, which prints the one-storey a the school model teaches; the book's own text face is a different font. Handwriting varies by writer. e: The Grundschrift-App was made in a research project of the Laborschule at Bielefeld University with the Grundschulverband, on its Grundschrift school model, with a teacher advisory team. Each letter is an ordered list of paths, one per pen-down stroke, which the app makes a child trace in order. It writes e in one stroke: from the middle left along the bar to the right, then anticlockwise up, over, down and round to the lower right. UJIpenchars2 (Prat, Castro, Llorens, Marzal and Vilar; UCI Machine Learning Repository dataset 177, CC BY 4.0) holds 120 tablet pen traces of e, two by each of 60 adult Spanish writers; only counts are cited. All 120 are one stroke; 90 start at the middle left, and all 120 turn anticlockwise. The app's repository has no licence, so only the order, the start, the direction and the lifts are taken from it; no point is copied, and the path is fitted to the e of the bundled LatinPrint-Subset.ttf, a renamed subset of SIL Global's literacy typeface Andika 7.000, which prints the one-storey a the school model teaches; the book's own text face is a different font. Handwriting varies by writer. n: The Grundschrift-App was made in a research project of the Laborschule at Bielefeld University with the Grundschulverband, on its Grundschrift school model, with a teacher advisory team. Each letter is an ordered list of paths, one per pen-down stroke, which the app makes a child trace in order. It writes n in one stroke: down the stem from the top, back up it, over the arch and down the right side. Grundschrift ends the stroke with a small hook to the right that the bundled outline does not print, so the path ends where the printed letter ends. UJIpenchars2 (Prat, Castro, Llorens, Marzal and Vilar; UCI Machine Learning Repository dataset 177, CC BY 4.0) holds 120 tablet pen traces of n, two by each of 60 adult Spanish writers; only counts are cited. 119 of the 120 are one stroke, and 74 of those 119 start at the top left (28 at the bottom left, as a joined hand does). The app's repository has no licence, so only the order, the start, the direction and the lifts are taken from it; no point is copied, and the path is fitted to the n of the bundled LatinPrint-Subset.ttf, a renamed subset of SIL Global's literacy typeface Andika 7.000, which prints the one-storey a the school model teaches; the book's own text face is a different font. Handwriting varies by writer. o: The Grundschrift-App was made in a research project of the Laborschule at Bielefeld University with the Grundschulverband, on its Grundschrift school model, with a teacher advisory team. Each letter is an ordered list of paths, one per pen-down stroke, which the app makes a child trace in order. It writes o in one stroke, from the top, anticlockwise, all the way round. UJIpenchars2 (Prat, Castro, Llorens, Marzal and Vilar; UCI Machine Learning Repository dataset 177, CC BY 4.0) holds 120 tablet pen traces of o, two by each of 60 adult Spanish writers; only counts are cited. All 120 are one stroke; 62 start at the top centre (24 top left, 23 top right), and 118 turn anticlockwise. The app's repository has no licence, so only the order, the start, the direction and the lifts are taken from it; no point is copied, and the path is fitted to the o of the bundled LatinPrint-Subset.ttf, a renamed subset of SIL Global's literacy typeface Andika 7.000, which prints the one-storey a the school model teaches; the book's own text face is a different font. Handwriting varies by writer. s: The Grundschrift-App was made in a research project of the Laborschule at Bielefeld University with the Grundschulverband, on its Grundschrift school model, with a teacher advisory team. Each letter is an ordered list of paths, one per pen-down stroke, which the app makes a child trace in order. It writes s in one stroke, from the top right: anticlockwise over the top, then clockwise round the bottom to the lower left. UJIpenchars2 (Prat, Castro, Llorens, Marzal and Vilar; UCI Machine Learning Repository dataset 177, CC BY 4.0) holds 120 tablet pen traces of s, two by each of 60 adult Spanish writers; only counts are cited. 117 of the 120 are one stroke, and 76 of those 117 start at the top right. The app's repository has no licence, so only the order, the start, the direction and the lifts are taken from it; no point is copied, and the path is fitted to the s of the bundled LatinPrint-Subset.ttf, a renamed subset of SIL Global's literacy typeface Andika 7.000, which prints the one-storey a the school model teaches; the book's own text face is a different font. Handwriting varies by writer. d: The Grundschrift-App was made in a research project of the Laborschule at Bielefeld University with the Grundschulverband, on its Grundschrift school model, with a teacher advisory team. Each letter is an ordered list of paths, one per pen-down stroke, which the app makes a child trace in order. It writes d in one stroke: anticlockwise round the bowl from the top right, up the stem to the top, and down it to the foot. UJIpenchars2 (Prat, Castro, Llorens, Marzal and Vilar; UCI Machine Learning Repository dataset 177, CC BY 4.0) holds 120 tablet pen traces of d, two by each of 60 adult Spanish writers; only counts are cited. 101 of the 120 are one stroke, the source's count (19 lift once), and 88 of those 101 go anticlockwise round the bowl first. The app's repository has no licence, so only the order, the start, the direction and the lifts are taken from it; no point is copied, and the path is fitted to the d of the bundled LatinPrint-Subset.ttf, a renamed subset of SIL Global's literacy typeface Andika 7.000, which prints the one-storey a the school model teaches; the book's own text face is a different font. Handwriting varies by writer. í: UJIpenchars2 (Prat, Castro, Llorens, Marzal and Vilar; UCI Machine Learning Repository dataset 177, CC BY 4.0) holds 120 tablet pen traces of í, two by each of 60 adult Spanish writers; only counts are cited. 117 are two strokes, because the accent takes the place of the dot. It is found as a separate mark in 69 of the 120 and drawn last in 66 of those 69; 44 of the 69 draw it up to the right, 16 down to the left. The i is the Grundschrift-App's i (level kleinbuchstaben/i, commit f6dbd80; no licence, facts only), with the acute in place of the dot. The accent is drawn up to the right, as most of these writers draw it; about three in ten draw it down to the left. Only counts and shares are cited; no trace is copied, and the path is fitted to the í of the bundled LatinPrint-Subset.ttf, a renamed subset of SIL Global's literacy typeface Andika 7.000, which prints the one-storey a the school model teaches; the book's own text face is a different font. Handwriting varies by writer. a: The Grundschrift-App was made in a research project of the Laborschule at Bielefeld University with the Grundschulverband, on its Grundschrift school model, with a teacher advisory team. Each letter is an ordered list of paths, one per pen-down stroke, which the app makes a child trace in order. It writes the one-storey a in one stroke: anticlockwise round the bowl from the top right, back up to the top of the stem, and down the stem to the foot. The printed a joins the bowl to the stem, so the path runs back up the stem to its top before it comes down, as the source does. UJIpenchars2 (Prat, Castro, Llorens, Marzal and Vilar; UCI Machine Learning Repository dataset 177, CC BY 4.0) holds 120 tablet pen traces of a, two by each of 60 adult Spanish writers; only counts are cited. 118 of the 120 are one stroke, the source's count; 92 of those 118 start at the top (72 top centre, 20 top right), and 111 go anticlockwise round the bowl. The app's repository has no licence, so only the order, the start, the direction and the lifts are taken from it; no point is copied, and the path is fitted to the a of the bundled LatinPrint-Subset.ttf, a renamed subset of SIL Global's literacy typeface Andika 7.000, which prints the one-storey a the school model teaches; the book's own text face is a different font. Handwriting varies by writer. s: The Grundschrift-App was made in a research project of the Laborschule at Bielefeld University with the Grundschulverband, on its Grundschrift school model, with a teacher advisory team. Each letter is an ordered list of paths, one per pen-down stroke, which the app makes a child trace in order. It writes s in one stroke, from the top right: anticlockwise over the top, then clockwise round the bottom to the lower left. UJIpenchars2 (Prat, Castro, Llorens, Marzal and Vilar; UCI Machine Learning Repository dataset 177, CC BY 4.0) holds 120 tablet pen traces of s, two by each of 60 adult Spanish writers; only counts are cited. 117 of the 120 are one stroke, and 76 of those 117 start at the top right. The app's repository has no licence, so only the order, the start, the direction and the lifts are taken from it; no point is copied, and the path is fitted to the s of the bundled LatinPrint-Subset.ttf, a renamed subset of SIL Global's literacy typeface Andika 7.000, which prints the one-storey a the school model teaches; the book's own text face is a different font. Handwriting varies by writer.
